29164249.extract:
# Ang Totoong Narcolist

**Ang Totoong Narcolist** (Filipino: The True Narcolist) is a YouTube video series created in April 2019 by Peter Joemel Advincula, a former member of a drug syndicate operating in the Philippines. The series featured a hooded whistleblower using the alias "Bikoy" who made allegations that members of President Rodrigo Duterte's family and close associates were involved in illegal drug trafficking. The videos generated significant national controversy and triggered numerous legal investigations, with various opposition politicians and civil society figures charged with sedition, though most charges were later dismissed or discontinued.

# Background

Peter Joemel Advincula was born in 1989 in Donsol, Sorsogon, Philippines. On May 6, 2010, he was introduced to a drug syndicate operating in Misibis Bay, a resort destination in Albay province. Within the organization, he was tasked with heading closed-circuit television operations in underground facilities and later assigned to prepare monthly documents called "TARA," which listed the collections and payoffs made that month. During his involvement with the syndicate, Advincula alleged that he witnessed the killing of one syndicate member and the rape of the member's family.

Fearing for his life after witnessing these crimes, Advincula fled the organization. He was subsequently apprehended by National Bureau of Investigation agents and, after attempting to flee, was arrested and convicted of fraud in 2012. He received a six-year prison sentence, spending his first three years at Naga City District Jail before being transferred to New Bilibid Prison due to good behavior. While imprisoned, Advincula engaged in religious activities and allegedly attempted to contact Senator Tito Sotto's office to expose the businessmen connected to the drug syndicate, though Sotto's office dismissed his claims as "suspicious." He was released in 2017 after serving five years, benefiting from a one-year reduction for good character.

# The Video Series

On April 2, 2019, Advincula created a YouTube channel titled "Ang Totoong Narcolist." The channel centered around a hooded figure claiming to be a former drug syndicate member who used the pseudonym "Bikoy." Over the course of one month, five videos were uploaded between April 2 and May 6, 2019. According to media analysis, the videos appeared professionally produced with quality annotation.

### Episode 1 (April 2)

The first episode displayed documents that "Bikoy" claimed were TARA records related to drug syndicate operations. These documents allegedly included dates, code names, bank accounts of high-ranking officials, and deposit records, with signatures purporting to verify the information's accuracy. "Bikoy" presented two code names, noting their similarity to actual criminal names. One was allegedly associated with Waldo Carpio, the brother of Sara Duterte's husband Mans Carpio, while another was claimed to belong to Paolo Duterte, with the accusation that Duterte bore a back tattoo displaying the code name.

### Episode 2 (April 7)

Released through Bombo Radyo Iloilo on April 7, the second episode presented additional code names allegedly associated with three bank accounts, including one belonging to Elijah Manuel Pepito, partner lawyer for Mans Carpio's law firm, and another to "Veronica Salvador," which "Bikoy" constructed by merging the names of Duterte's domestic partner Honeylet Avanceña and their daughter Kitty (born Veronica).

### Episode 3 (April 8)

The third episode, released on YouTube on April 8, focused on allegations against Senator Bong Go, claiming that drug proceeds were being funneled to his bank accounts and that Go bore a dragon tattoo with his alleged code name.

### Episode 4 (April 12)

In the fourth episode, "Bikoy" reiterated claims about Go's tattoo and displayed a photograph of Go playing basketball, pointing out a portion of what he claimed was a dragon tattoo visible on Go's back. He also reaffirmed Carpio's alleged involvement in drug operations.

### Episode 5 (April 22)

The final episode, released on April 22, identified organizations allegedly connected to the Misibis Bay syndicate and presented the "Quadrangle Group," described as an alleged organization of wealthy businessmen engaged in drug operations. Among those named were businessman Elizaldy Co, Albay Representative Fernando Gonzalez, Camarines Norte Governor Edgardo Tallado, former congressman and governor Luis Villafuerte, Catanduanes Governor Joseph Cua, Sorsogon provincial board member Krunimar Escudero, businessman Victor Lorenzo Rosales, Naga businessman Thomas Enrile, and businesswoman Tess Rañola.

# Government Response and Investigation

### Initial Reaction

The Duterte administration quickly rejected the allegations. Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo characterized the claims as "black propaganda" and dismissed "Bikoy" as a "pawn." President Duterte blamed the political opposition and suggested that Senator Antonio Trillanes was likely behind the videos, making derogatory comments about Trillanes. The Liberal Party publicly denied involvement in creating the videos. The Department of Justice questioned "Bikoy's" credibility, citing his anonymity as a significant concern.

The President challenged Paolo Duterte to display the alleged tattoo, which Duterte refused to do. Communist Party of the Philippines founder Jose Maria Sison called for "Bikoy" to be granted protection to tell his story, though this voice stood alone among government officials.

### Rodel Jayme Arrest

Rodel Jayme, who owned a website that distributed the videos, was apprehended on April 30, 2019. Jayme subsequently faced charges of inciting sedition in connection with the distribution of the materials.

### The Oust Duterte Matrix

On April 22, 2019, the same day the fifth video was released, Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo announced the release of the "Oust Duterte matrix," a diagram purporting to show links between journalists, civil society organizations, and alleged plots to overthrow President Duterte. Panelo claimed the matrix had undergone "proper validation." The diagram named journalists affiliated with prominent news organizations including the Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism and Rappler. Many individuals included in the matrix subsequently denied involvement in any ouster plot, while one affected group sought government protection from harassment.

# Advincula's Disclosure and Recantation

On May 6, 2019, Advincula surfaced publicly at the headquarters of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines, identifying himself as "Bikoy" and requesting legal assistance. He stated that he had decided to reveal his identity because of threats to his safety and his conscience regarding the destruction caused by drug trafficking, in which he had once participated. He emphasized that the documents shown in the videos were authentic and contained details about drug syndicate operations dating back to 2010.

On May 22, 2019, just 16 days after publicly identifying himself, Advincula surrendered to police. During a televised press conference, he recanted his previous allegations, stating that he had played a role in a script created by the Liberal Party. Following this recantation, he requested protective custody, claiming that his life was in danger. On June 3, 2019, Advincula turned himself over to police for protection, and he was released from protective custody on June 25, 2019.

# Legal Proceedings

### Against Opposition Figures

On May 17, 2019, the Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group filed multiple criminal complaints against various opposition politicians and civil society figures, including Vice President Leonor Robredo, Senator Antonio Trillanes IV, and numerous others. The charges included sedition, inciting to sedition, cyber libel, libel, estafa, harboring a criminal, and obstruction of justice.

Following investigation, the Department of Justice initially pursued the case against Trillanes and eleven others on a charge of conspiracy to commit sedition, while clearing Vice President Robredo on February 10, 2020, citing lack of probable cause. The sedition charges against most other defendants were also dismissed, though the DOJ continued prosecuting the conspiracy to commit sedition case against Trillanes and a smaller group of co-accused.

### Against Advincula

In July 2019, Advincula filed a sworn affidavit alleging that three lawyers—Jose Manuel I. Diokno, Theodore O. Te, and Lorenzo R. Tañada III—were part of a group called "Project Sodoma" that plotted to commit sedition, cyber libel, and libel, and that they met with him at Ateneo de Manila University. The three lawyers denied the allegations, stating that they were present at the location for a senatorial candidates forum, not to meet with Advincula. Charges of sedition were subsequently filed against opposition members based on Advincula's affidavit, though these charges were later dismissed as the Department of Justice determined that Advincula himself was probably guilty of conspiracy to commit sedition.

On May 22, 2023, the Manila Metropolitan Trial Court Branch 17 found Advincula guilty beyond reasonable doubt of perjury in connection with the false statements he made in his July 2019 affidavit regarding the three lawyers. The court sentenced him to an indeterminate penalty of three months and one day to one year and one day of imprisonment.

### Against Private Citizens and Platforms

Elizaldy Co, the prominent Bicolano businessman named in the fifth video as the alleged leader of the Quadrangle Group, and Misibis Bay Resort jointly filed a one billion Philippine peso cyber libel suit against Facebook, YouTube, Advincula, and others in May 2019. Co claimed that the allegations damaged his business reputation and resulted in a bank suspending the processing of a significant loan application. Co characterized the video's content as false and stated that Misibis Bay Resort had never been used for illegal drug operations or as a drug laboratory. This marked the first cyber libel suit filed in the Philippines against major social media platforms.

# Legacy and Aftermath

The "Ang Totoong Narcolist" videos occurred during a period of intense political tension in the Philippines, coinciding with the 2019 midterm elections scheduled for May 13, 2019, just days after the first video's release. The controversy highlighted broader divisions over President Duterte's drug war policy, with critics alleging that the campaign was being used to eliminate rivals while protecting allies allegedly involved in the drug trade, while administration supporters viewed the videos as part of a political attack on the presidency.

The series demonstrated the potential for viral online content to trigger political upheaval, prompt government investigations, and result in subsequent legal proceedings affecting multiple individuals across the political spectrum. The recantation by Advincula, the subsequent perjury conviction, and the dismissal of charges against most opposition figures complicated the narrative surrounding the videos and raised questions about the reliability of the allegations presented.

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=0&oldformat=true)On April 2, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula, a former criminal, created a series of videos titled **"Ang Totoong Narcolist"** (transl. The True Narcolist). It discussed the alleged involvement of the [Duterte family](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Duterte_family "Duterte family") in drug syndicates, accusing politicians [Bong Go](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bong_Go "Bong Go") and [Paolo Duterte](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), both closely related to the Duterte family. The videos garnered nationwide attention as politicians denied the accusations; a manhunt was also commenced.

During Advincula's childhood, he wanted to become a priest; he was introduced to a drug [syndicate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Syndicate "Syndicate"), which led to him being charged with [fraud](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Fraud "Fraud") in 2012. Advincula had to remain in prison for six years; he was released one year early in 2017 due to [good character](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time"). After dwelling in prison, Advincula wanted to become a [whistleblower](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Whistleblowing "Whistleblowing"). He created a channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" in YouTube on April 2, 2019, based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy". Five videos were produced, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6. The videos induced a manhunt for the perpetrator led by the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)"). Originally, Rodel Jayme, the owner of a website which distributed the videos, was apprehended on April 30. Just before Jayme was convicted, Advincula surrendered to the police. He paid his bail and left [Camp Crame](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Camp_Crame "Camp Crame"), where he was detained, yet returned to the police for protection. Numerous politicians were charged with sedition, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo") and Trillanes. The [Oust Duterte matrix](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Oust_Duterte_matrix "Oust Duterte matrix"), a diagram exhibiting participants of an alleged ouster plot, was released on April 22, soon after the controversy.

### Perpetrator

Advincula was born in 1989, in [Donsol](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Donsol "Donsol"), Sorsogon, Philippines. He was introduced to a drug syndicate operating in [Misibis Bay](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Misibis_Bay "Misibis Bay") on May 6, 2010, and was selected to head [closed-circuit television](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Closed-circuit_television "Closed-circuit television") operations in underground facilities throughout the area. After, he was tasked to prepare the monthly "TARA", a document listing the collections and payoffs that month.[\[1\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) During this time, Advincula allegedly witnessed the killing of one of his syndicate members, as well as the raping of the latter's wife and daughter.[\[2\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020133-2)

[![Image 1: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg/640px-President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#/media/File:President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_\(cropped\).jpg)

A portrait of President Rodrigo Duterte

Advincula fled the syndicate due to a fear that he would be murdered. Eventually, [National Bureau of Investigation](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) agents found Advincula. He attempted to run from them but was arrested, convicted of fraud in 2012, and sentenced to six years in prison. During the first three years, he was detained at the [Naga City](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Naga,_Camarines_Sur "Naga, Camarines Sur") District Jail. He was transferred to the [New Bilibid Prison](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/New_Bilibid_Prison "New Bilibid Prison") due to good behavior. In prison, he returned to his religious activities, serving as a "teacher" for the local detainees.[\[1\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) Allegedly, during his detainment, he contacted the office of Senator [Tito Sotto](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Tito_Sotto "Tito Sotto"). He attempted to expose the businessmen who connected him to the drug syndicate to leave the prison. Sotto did not reply, finding his claims "suspicious."[\[3\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He was released in 2017, one year early due to good character.[\[1\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1)

### Duterte administration

Rodrigo Duterte won the [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election") and assumed presidency on June 30.[\[4\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-4) His presidency was controversial and marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte's_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people under Duterte's command. This drew condemnation from the [United Nations](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/European_Union "European Union"), and other international organizations.[\[5\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-5) Large protests have also been held against the administration of Duterte; many of them were against the PNP killings.[\[6\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-6) In September 2018, an alleged ouster plot, titled [Red October](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Red_October_/(plot/) "Red October (plot)"), was allegedly found, reportedly created by members of the opposition.[\[7\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-7) In March 2019, Duterte exposed 46 "narcolists," or politicians with connections to drug syndicates.[\[8\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-8) Along with this, various disinformation campaigns were created leading up to the [2019 Philippine general election](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/2019_Philippine_general_election "2019 Philippine general election").[\[9\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-9) [Surigao del Norte](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Surigao_del_Norte "Surigao del Norte") Representative [Ace Barbers](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ace_Barbers "Ace Barbers") portrayed these scandals as a possible motive for the creation of the "Bikoy" videos.[\[10\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-10)

[![Image 2: Thumb](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/67/Bikoyvideostill.jpg/320px-Bikoyvideostill.jpg)](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#/media/File:Bikoyvideostill.jpg)

Still from _[The Philippine Star](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/The_Philippine_Star "The Philippine Star")_ showing the hooded figure in an episode of the "Bikoy" series

In August 2018, Advincula planned to go into hiding and become a whistleblower; he wanted to expose the Misibis Bay syndicate's operations.[\[1\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) He created a YouTube channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist), set up on April 2, 2019. The videos are based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy", who claimed to be a former member of drug syndicates in [Southern Luzon](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Southern_Luzon "Southern Luzon") and the [Visayas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Visayas "Visayas") archipelago. According to _[Vera Files](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Vera_Files "Vera Files")_, the videos seemed professionally done and had nice annotation.[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) Five videos were created in total, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6; the videos were widely circulated throughout social media.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

The first episode was released on April 2.[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) It displayed papers that "Bikoy" claimed to be TARA documents related to the syndicate. According to "Bikoy", typical TARA documents contain a date, a code name and bank account of a high-ranking official, and deposits made. The bottom of the documents flaunted a signature which ensured that the details in the documents were accurate. "Bikoy" then presented two code names, saying that the code names were not "so bright" due to their similarity to criminals' real names. He claimed the first code name was associated with Waldo Carpio, the brother of [Sara Duterte's](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") husband, [Mans Carpio](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mans_Carpio "Mans Carpio").[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[\[14\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-14) He then purported that the other code name belonged to [Paolo Duterte](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), alleging that the latter had a tattoo on his back showing the code name.[\[15\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15)

The second episode was released five days later[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)[\[11\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) through [Bombo Radyo Iloilo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bombo_Radyo_Iloilo "Bombo Radyo Iloilo"). It divulged a new code name, which according to "Bikoy", was difficult to trace. He eventually associated the names to three bank accounts, including one belonging to Elijah Manuel Pepito and another to Veronica Salvador. Pepito was the partner lawyer for Mans Carpio's law firm. "Veronica Salvador" was a merged name of Duterte's wife, [Honeylet "Salvador" Avanceña](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña"), and their daughter Kitty, shown as "Veronica".[\[16\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-16)

The third episode was released on April 8, the following day,[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) on [YouTube](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/YouTube "YouTube").[\[17\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-17) It discussed the alleged involvement of Senator [Bong Go](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Bong_Go "Bong Go") in the drug trade. "Bikoy" claimed that drug money was being funneled to Go's account and insisted that Go had a dragon tattoo on his back with his code name.[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) The fourth episode was released on April 12, four days later.[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) In the video, "Bikoy" further argued that Go had a dragon tattoo and stated that he was confident of his allegation; he showed a picture of Go playing basketball with a portion of the dragon tattoo visible. In the video, he reiterated that Carpio was involved in drug operations.[\[19\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-19) The fifth and final video was released on April 22. In it, "Bikoy" revealed alleged organizations related to the Misibis Bay syndicate and identified personalities he claimed were involved. He also exhibited the "Quadrangle Group", an alleged group of rich businessmen allegedly involved in drug operations.[\[13\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)

Numerous Duterte-aligned politicians opposed the videos. During the episodes' release, [Presidential Spokesperson](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Presidential_spokesperson_/(Philippines/) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)") [Salvador Panelo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") said that the allegations mentioned were "[black propaganda](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Black_propaganda "Black propaganda")" and that "Bikoy" was just a "pawn." He also accused the [Liberal Party of the Philippines](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Liberal_Party_/(Philippines/) "Liberal Party (Philippines)") of creating the videos.[\[20\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-20) After the first video, President Duterte blamed the political opposition and hinted that Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") was likely behind it, calling him [gay](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Gay "Gay").[\[21\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-21) Due to Advincula's allegations that Bong Go has a dragon tattoo, Go has shown his back on two occasions: at a [Hugpong ng Pagbabago](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Hugpong_ng_Pagbabago "Hugpong ng Pagbabago") campaign event[\[18\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) and later at a [Luntiang Pilipinas](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Luntiang_Pilipinas "Luntiang Pilipinas") campaign event in [Calamba, Laguna](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Calamba,_Laguna "Calamba, Laguna").[\[22\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-22) Trillanes praised the videos, wishing to have been part of the videos' creation. He then challenged [Paolo Duterte](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte") to display the tattoo on his back, which Duterte refused to do.[\[15\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15) The Liberal Party denied their involvement[\[23\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-23) while [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines") founder [Jose Maria Sison](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison") said "Bikoy" should be given protection to tell his story.[\[24\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-24) The [Department of Justice of the Philippines](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Department_of_Justice_/(Philippines/) "Department of Justice (Philippines)") (DOJ) questioned "Bikoy"'s credibility due to his anonymity.[\[25\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-25) The videos were considered a controversial topic online: viewers shared documents from the video, with a [Facebook](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Facebook "Facebook") page titled "for the motherland Sass Rogando Sasot" encountering connections between the documents shown to a bank in [Legazpi, Albay](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Legazpi,_Albay "Legazpi, Albay").[\[26\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-26) According to the [Philippine News Agency](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philippine_News_Agency "Philippine News Agency"), the videos were "publicly viewed, shared and uploaded" multiple times.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

### Oust Duterte matrix

Shortly after the release of the videos, specifically on April 16, Duterte reported in a speech that he had received intelligence reports detailing an alleged ouster plot. Six days later, Panelo released the "Oust Duterte matrix," on the president's orders. The matrix named journalists from several news outlets, particularly the [Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") and _[Rappler](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Rappler "Rappler")_. Panelo said those journalists could be feeding their stories to "enemies of the state," or the opposition. He stated that the matrix was released to expose those behind the alleged ouster plot and did not file charges against the journalists shown in the matrix.[\[27\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-27)

Manhunt and investigation
-------------------------

### Rodel Jayme's arrest

The DOJ began investigating the videos April 17.[\[28\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) The cybercrime division of the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) said that the website "metrobalita.net", a page which shared the videos, was owned by blogger Rodel Jayme. He was arrested in his residence in [Parañaque](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque") April 30 and detained in NBI headquarters.[\[29\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:4-29) Jayme was them charged with [sedition](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Sedition "Sedition") on May 2, with DOJ Secretary [Menardo Guevarra](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Menardo_Guevarra "Menardo Guevarra") saying he could also be charged with child abuse for mentioning Duterte's daughter in one of the videos.[\[28\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) Jayme accused opposition groups of forcing him to create the websites. An NBI spokesperson said that Jayme could be a state witness for the accusations.[\[30\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-30)

### Peter Advincula's arrest

Just before Jayme was to be charged, Peter Advincula, the original "Bikoy", emerged. He requested help from the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Integrated_Bar_of_the_Philippines "Integrated Bar of the Philippines") (IBP) in suing the Dutertes and their allies,[\[31\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-31) maintaining his allegations were true. Two days later, the IBP rejected his offer. He then asked Senator [Panfilo Lacson](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Panfilo_Lacson "Panfilo Lacson") to postpone his hearing until the elections.[\[32\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-32) That same day, Guevarra gave Advincula an ultimatum: bring evidence to back up his claims in the videos to the NBI, or face sedition charges.[\[33\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-33) Advincula surrendered to police May 22, stating on national television that he played a role in a script made by the Liberal Party.[\[34\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020132-36) The media called this reversal "[flip-flopping](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Flip-flop_/(politics/) "Flip-flop (politics)")".[\[3\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He also accused Trillanes of taking part in the video's production.[\[37\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-37) The DOJ said that his allegations would need a deep investigation.[\[38\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-38) [Solicitor General](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Solicitor_General_of_the_Philippines "Solicitor General of the Philippines") [Jose Calida](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Jose_Calida "Jose Calida") offered legal aid to Advincula.[\[39\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-39) Advincula had his [mugshot](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Mug_shot "Mug shot") on May 23.[\[40\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-40) [Elizaldy Co](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Elizaldy_Co "Elizaldy Co"), one of the people mentioned in the videos, filed a 1 billion PHP lawsuit for damage from the accusations relating to him.[\[41\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-41)

The next day, Advincula, charged with for six counts of [estafa](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Fraud "Fraud"), paid 6,000 [PHP](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso") in bail.[\[42\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-42) The next day, he left Camp Crame, where he was detained.[\[43\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-43) The [Philippine National Police](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) started an investigation against Advincula[\[44\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-44) yet skipped a case hearing on the investigation the following day.[\[45\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-45) He turned himself in to the police for protection on June 3, claiming that his life was in danger.[\[46\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-46) The next day, the DOJ concluded their investigation, charging him with fraud, without a statement from Advincula.[\[47\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-47) Trillanes released texts from Advincula for the production of the videos.[\[48\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-48) Advincula was released from protective custody on June 25.[\[49\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-49) [Ako Bicol](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ako_Bicol "Ako Bicol") Representative [Alfredo Garbin](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Alfredo_Garbin "Alfredo Garbin") filed a resolution on May 29 for the [Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Philippine_House_Committee_on_Information_and_Communications_Technology "Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology") to investigate the potential effects of misinformation on social media platforms due to the videos.[\[12\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12) The resolution resulted in investigations against Facebook and Google and a request for both to attend the hearing.[\[50\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-50)

### Lawsuits

Numerous politicians were sued for sedition on July 18, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo").[\[51\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-51) Investigations began into his and other politicians' connection to the "Bikoy" videos.[\[52\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-52) Advincula surrendered again to the PNP July 29.[\[53\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-53)[\[54\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-54) He posted 10,000 PHP bail two days later[\[55\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-55) and then applied for state protection on August 5 with his lawyer [Larry Gadon](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Larry_Gadon "Larry Gadon").[\[56\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-56) Two Catholic bishops were also charged with sedition later that month due to an alleged conversation with Advincula.[\[57\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-57) On August 20, Calida linked the videos to servers in the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University").[\[58\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-58) Robredo responded to the investigations with a counter-affidavit, denying the accusations on August 29.[\[59\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-59) In September, a former lawyer of Trillanes stated that the senator had ties to "Bikoy"; the senator denied the accusation.[\[60\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-60) On February 10, 2020, Robredo was cleared of the charges against her, while [Antonio Trillanes](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") and actor [Joel Saracho](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Joel_Saracho "Joel Saracho"), among others, were charged with sedition.[\[61\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-61)

Aftermath and legacy
--------------------

On January 20, 2021, Advincula was charged with [perjury](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Perjury "Perjury") by a Manila court for allegedly false statements against the [Free Legal Assistance Group](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Free_Legal_Assistance_Group "Free Legal Assistance Group").[\[62\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-62)[\[63\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-63) A warrant was issued for his arrest.[\[64\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-64) He surrendered at a local police station in [Daraga](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Daraga "Daraga"), posting 18,000 PHP bail.[\[65\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-65) He was absent from the court on July 21, causing the court to reissue his arrest warrant due to Advincula being unable to justify his absence.[\[66\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-66) Advincula allegedly killed three politicians in [Albay](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Albay "Albay") on November 13, with their bodies appearing in his [ukay-ukay](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ukay-ukay "Ukay-ukay") store in Daraga. He was declared the primary suspect.[\[67\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-67)[\[68\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-68) According to local police, his possible motive was a grudge between him and one of the victims after the man rejected Advincula's request for a loan.[\[69\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-69) He posted the 1 million PHP bail on December 16.[\[70\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-70) Two years later, he was convicted of perjury in statements he made in 2019 implicating lawyers [Erin Tañada](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Erin_Ta%C3%B1ada "Erin Tañada"), [Chel Diokno](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Chel_Diokno "Chel Diokno"), and [Theodore Te](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Theodore_Te "Theodore Te") in an ouster plot.[\[71\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-71)[\[72\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-72) He was sentenced to a maximum of one year and one day in prison.[\[73\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-73) but eventually posted bail soon after the verdict.[\[74\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-74) In 2020, a journal released by the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University") detailed the videos.[\[75\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020126-75) On October 8, 2024, Advincula filed his candidacy for senator in the [2025 election](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/2025_Philippine_Senate_election "2025 Philippine Senate election"), pushing for a centralized correctional system in the Philippines[\[76\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-76)[\[77\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-77) but he was declared a [nuisance candidate](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Nuisance_candidate "Nuisance candidate") by the [Commission on Elections](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Commission_on_Elections_/(Philippines/) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)").[\[78\]](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/articles/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-78)

[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

On April 2, 2019, Peter Joemel Advincula, a former criminal, created a series of videos titled **"Ang Totoong Narcolist"** (transl. The True Narcolist). It discussed the alleged involvement of the [Duterte family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duterte_family "Duterte family") in drug syndicates, accusing politicians [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go") and [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), both closely related to the Duterte family. The videos garnered nationwide attention as politicians denied the accusations; a manhunt was also commenced.

During Advincula's childhood, he wanted to become a priest; he was introduced to a drug [syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicate "Syndicate"), which led to him being charged with [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") in 2012. Advincula had to remain in prison for six years; he was released one year early in 2017 due to [good character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time"). After dwelling in prison, Advincula wanted to become a [whistleblower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistleblowing "Whistleblowing"). He created a channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" in YouTube on April 2, 2019, based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy". Five videos were produced, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6. The videos induced a manhunt for the perpetrator led by the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)"). Originally, Rodel Jayme, the owner of a website which distributed the videos, was apprehended on April 30. Just before Jayme was convicted, Advincula surrendered to the police. He paid his bail and left [Camp Crame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Crame "Camp Crame"), where he was detained, yet returned to the police for protection. Numerous politicians were charged with sedition, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo") and Trillanes. The [Oust Duterte matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix "Oust Duterte matrix"), a diagram exhibiting participants of an alleged ouster plot, was released on April 22, soon after the controversy.

Advincula was born in 1989, in [Donsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donsol "Donsol"), Sorsogon, Philippines. He was introduced to a drug syndicate operating in [Misibis Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misibis_Bay "Misibis Bay") on May 6, 2010, and was selected to head [closed-circuit television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed-circuit_television "Closed-circuit television") operations in underground facilities throughout the area. After, he was tasked to prepare the monthly "TARA", a document listing the collections and payoffs that month.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) During this time, Advincula allegedly witnessed the killing of one of his syndicate members, as well as the raping of the latter's wife and daughter.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020133-2)

[![Image 2: Refer to caption](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Rodrigo_Duterte_portrait_/(cropped/).jpg)

A portrait of President Rodrigo Duterte

Advincula fled the syndicate due to a fear that he would be murdered. Eventually, [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) agents found Advincula. He attempted to run from them but was arrested, convicted of fraud in 2012, and sentenced to six years in prison. During the first three years, he was detained at the [Naga City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naga,_Camarines_Sur "Naga, Camarines Sur") District Jail. He was transferred to the [New Bilibid Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Bilibid_Prison "New Bilibid Prison") due to good behavior. In prison, he returned to his religious activities, serving as a "teacher" for the local detainees.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) Allegedly, during his detainment, he contacted the office of Senator [Tito Sotto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Sotto "Tito Sotto"). He attempted to expose the businessmen who connected him to the drug syndicate to leave the prison. Sotto did not reply, finding his claims "suspicious."[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He was released in 2017, one year early due to good character.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1)

### Duterte administration

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Duterte administration")\]

Rodrigo Duterte won the [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election") and assumed presidency on June 30.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-4) His presidency was controversial and marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people under Duterte's command. This drew condemnation from the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other international organizations.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-5) Large protests have also been held against the administration of Duterte; many of them were against the PNP killings.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-6) In September 2018, an alleged ouster plot, titled [Red October](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_/(plot/) "Red October (plot)"), was allegedly found, reportedly created by members of the opposition.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-7) In March 2019, Duterte exposed 46 "narcolists," or politicians with connections to drug syndicates.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-8) Along with this, various disinformation campaigns were created leading up to the [2019 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Philippine_general_election "2019 Philippine general election").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-9) [Surigao del Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surigao_del_Norte "Surigao del Norte") Representative [Ace Barbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_Barbers "Ace Barbers") portrayed these scandals as a possible motive for the creation of the "Bikoy" videos.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-10)

[![Image 3: A hooded figure staring in a black background](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/67/Bikoyvideostill.jpg/250px-Bikoyvideostill.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bikoyvideostill.jpg)

Still from _[The Philippine Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Philippine_Star "The Philippine Star")_ showing the hooded figure in an episode of the "Bikoy" series

In August 2018, Advincula planned to go into hiding and become a whistleblower; he wanted to expose the Misibis Bay syndicate's operations.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:0-1) He created a YouTube channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist), set up on April 2, 2019. The videos are based around a hooded whistleblower named "Bikoy", who claimed to be a former member of drug syndicates in [Southern Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Luzon "Southern Luzon") and the [Visayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visayas "Visayas") archipelago. According to _[Vera Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Files "Vera Files")_, the videos seemed professionally done and had nice annotation.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) Five videos were created in total, between April 2 and Advincula's surrender on May 6; the videos were widely circulated throughout social media.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

The first episode was released on April 2.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) It displayed papers that "Bikoy" claimed to be TARA documents related to the syndicate. According to "Bikoy", typical TARA documents contain a date, a code name and bank account of a high-ranking official, and deposits made. The bottom of the documents flaunted a signature which ensured that the details in the documents were accurate. "Bikoy" then presented two code names, saying that the code names were not "so bright" due to their similarity to criminals' real names. He claimed the first code name was associated with Waldo Carpio, the brother of [Sara Duterte's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") husband, [Mans Carpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mans_Carpio "Mans Carpio").[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-14) He then purported that the other code name belonged to [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte"), alleging that the latter had a tattoo on his back showing the code name.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15)

The second episode was released five days later[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:1-11) through [Bombo Radyo Iloilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombo_Radyo_Iloilo "Bombo Radyo Iloilo"). It divulged a new code name, which according to "Bikoy", was difficult to trace. He eventually associated the names to three bank accounts, including one belonging to Elijah Manuel Pepito and another to Veronica Salvador. Pepito was the partner lawyer for Mans Carpio's law firm. "Veronica Salvador" was a merged name of Duterte's wife, [Honeylet "Salvador" Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña"), and their daughter Kitty, shown as "Veronica".[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-16)

The third episode was released on April 8, the following day,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-17) It discussed the alleged involvement of Senator [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go") in the drug trade. "Bikoy" claimed that drug money was being funneled to Go's account and insisted that Go had a dragon tattoo on his back with his code name.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) The fourth episode was released on April 12, four days later.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13) In the video, "Bikoy" further argued that Go had a dragon tattoo and stated that he was confident of his allegation; he showed a picture of Go playing basketball with a portion of the dragon tattoo visible. In the video, he reiterated that Carpio was involved in drug operations.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-19) The fifth and final video was released on April 22. In it, "Bikoy" revealed alleged organizations related to the Misibis Bay syndicate and identified personalities he claimed were involved. He also exhibited the "Quadrangle Group", an alleged group of rich businessmen allegedly involved in drug operations.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:2-13)

Numerous Duterte-aligned politicians opposed the videos. During the episodes' release, [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_/(Philippines/) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)") [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") said that the allegations mentioned were "[black propaganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_propaganda "Black propaganda")" and that "Bikoy" was just a "pawn." He also accused the [Liberal Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_/(Philippines/) "Liberal Party (Philippines)") of creating the videos.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-20) After the first video, President Duterte blamed the political opposition and hinted that Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") was likely behind it, calling him [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-21) Due to Advincula's allegations that Bong Go has a dragon tattoo, Go has shown his back on two occasions: at a [Hugpong ng Pagbabago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugpong_ng_Pagbabago "Hugpong ng Pagbabago") campaign event[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:3-18) and later at a [Luntiang Pilipinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luntiang_Pilipinas "Luntiang Pilipinas") campaign event in [Calamba, Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calamba,_Laguna "Calamba, Laguna").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-22) Trillanes praised the videos, wishing to have been part of the videos' creation. He then challenged [Paolo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte") to display the tattoo on his back, which Duterte refused to do.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:8-15) The Liberal Party denied their involvement[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-23) while [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines") founder [Jose Maria Sison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison") said "Bikoy" should be given protection to tell his story.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-24) The [Department of Justice of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Justice_/(Philippines/) "Department of Justice (Philippines)") (DOJ) questioned "Bikoy"'s credibility due to his anonymity.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-25) The videos were considered a controversial topic online: viewers shared documents from the video, with a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") page titled "for the motherland Sass Rogando Sasot" encountering connections between the documents shown to a bank in [Legazpi, Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legazpi,_Albay "Legazpi, Albay").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-26) According to the [Philippine News Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_News_Agency "Philippine News Agency"), the videos were "publicly viewed, shared and uploaded" multiple times.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12)

### Oust Duterte matrix

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Oust Duterte matrix")\]

Shortly after the release of the videos, specifically on April 16, Duterte reported in a speech that he had received intelligence reports detailing an alleged ouster plot. Six days later, Panelo released the "Oust Duterte matrix," on the president's orders. The matrix named journalists from several news outlets, particularly the [Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") and _[Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler")_. Panelo said those journalists could be feeding their stories to "enemies of the state," or the opposition. He stated that the matrix was released to expose those behind the alleged ouster plot and did not file charges against the journalists shown in the matrix.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-27)

Manhunt and investigation
-------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Manhunt and investigation")\]

### Rodel Jayme's arrest

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Rodel Jayme's arrest")\]

The DOJ began investigating the videos April 17.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) The cybercrime division of the [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_/(Philippines/) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") (NBI) said that the website "metrobalita.net", a page which shared the videos, was owned by blogger Rodel Jayme. He was arrested in his residence in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque") April 30 and detained in NBI headquarters.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:4-29) Jayme was them charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition") on May 2, with DOJ Secretary [Menardo Guevarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menardo_Guevarra "Menardo Guevarra") saying he could also be charged with child abuse for mentioning Duterte's daughter in one of the videos.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:5-28) Jayme accused opposition groups of forcing him to create the websites. An NBI spokesperson said that Jayme could be a state witness for the accusations.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-30)

### Peter Advincula's arrest

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Peter Advincula's arrest")\]

Just before Jayme was to be charged, Peter Advincula, the original "Bikoy", emerged. He requested help from the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Bar_of_the_Philippines "Integrated Bar of the Philippines") (IBP) in suing the Dutertes and their allies,[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-31) maintaining his allegations were true. Two days later, the IBP rejected his offer. He then asked Senator [Panfilo Lacson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panfilo_Lacson "Panfilo Lacson") to postpone his hearing until the elections.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-32) That same day, Guevarra gave Advincula an ultimatum: bring evidence to back up his claims in the videos to the NBI, or face sedition charges.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-33) Advincula surrendered to police May 22, stating on national television that he played a role in a script made by the Liberal Party.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAlejo2020132-36) The media called this reversal "[flip-flopping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip-flop_/(politics/) "Flip-flop (politics)")".[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:7-3) He also accused Trillanes of taking part in the video's production.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-37) The DOJ said that his allegations would need a deep investigation.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-38) [Solicitor General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_the_Philippines "Solicitor General of the Philippines") [Jose Calida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Calida "Jose Calida") offered legal aid to Advincula.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-39) Advincula had his [mugshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mug_shot "Mug shot") on May 23.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-40) [Elizaldy Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizaldy_Co "Elizaldy Co"), one of the people mentioned in the videos, filed a 1 billion PHP lawsuit for damage from the accusations relating to him.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-41)

The next day, Advincula, charged with for six counts of [estafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud"), paid 6,000 [PHP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso") in bail.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-42) The next day, he left Camp Crame, where he was detained.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-43) The [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) started an investigation against Advincula[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-44) yet skipped a case hearing on the investigation the following day.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-45) He turned himself in to the police for protection on June 3, claiming that his life was in danger.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-46) The next day, the DOJ concluded their investigation, charging him with fraud, without a statement from Advincula.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-47) Trillanes released texts from Advincula for the production of the videos.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-48) Advincula was released from protective custody on June 25.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-49) [Ako Bicol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ako_Bicol "Ako Bicol") Representative [Alfredo Garbin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Garbin "Alfredo Garbin") filed a resolution on May 29 for the [Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_House_Committee_on_Information_and_Communications_Technology "Philippine House Committee on Information and Communications Technology") to investigate the potential effects of misinformation on social media platforms due to the videos.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-:6-12) The resolution resulted in investigations against Facebook and Google and a request for both to attend the hearing.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-50)

Numerous politicians were sued for sedition on July 18, including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo").[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-51) Investigations began into his and other politicians' connection to the "Bikoy" videos.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-52) Advincula surrendered again to the PNP July 29.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-53)[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-54) He posted 10,000 PHP bail two days later[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-55) and then applied for state protection on August 5 with his lawyer [Larry Gadon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Gadon "Larry Gadon").[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-56) Two Catholic bishops were also charged with sedition later that month due to an alleged conversation with Advincula.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-57) On August 20, Calida linked the videos to servers in the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University").[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-58) Robredo responded to the investigations with a counter-affidavit, denying the accusations on August 29.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-59) In September, a former lawyer of Trillanes stated that the senator had ties to "Bikoy"; the senator denied the accusation.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-60) On February 10, 2020, Robredo was cleared of the charges against her, while [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") and actor [Joel Saracho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Saracho "Joel Saracho"), among others, were charged with sedition.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-61)

Aftermath and legacy
--------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ang_Totoong_Narcolist&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Aftermath and legacy")\]

On January 20, 2021, Advincula was charged with [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") by a Manila court for allegedly false statements against the [Free Legal Assistance Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Legal_Assistance_Group "Free Legal Assistance Group").[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-62)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-63) A warrant was issued for his arrest.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-64) He surrendered at a local police station in [Daraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraga "Daraga"), posting 18,000 PHP bail.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-65) He was absent from the court on July 21, causing the court to reissue his arrest warrant due to Advincula being unable to justify his absence.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-66) Advincula allegedly killed three politicians in [Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albay "Albay") on November 13, with their bodies appearing in his [ukay-ukay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukay-ukay "Ukay-ukay") store in Daraga. He was declared the primary suspect.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-67)[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-68) According to local police, his possible motive was a grudge between him and one of the victims after the man rejected Advincula's request for a loan.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-69) He posted the 1 million PHP bail on December 16.[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist#cite_note-70) Two years later, he was convicted of perjury in statements he made in 2019 implicating lawyers [Erin Tañada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_Ta%C3%B1ada "Erin Tañada"), [Chel Diokno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chel_Diokno "Chel Diokno"), and [Theodore Te](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Te "Theodore Te") in an ouster THE man claiming to be Bikoy, the hooded figure in a series of anti-Duterte videos, has surrendered again.

This time, Peter Joemel Advincula's surrender is related to the cyber libel charges filed against him by Bicol-based businessman Zaldy Co, the owner of the posh Misibis Bay Resort.

Advincula had linked Co to the illegal drugs trade in the videos called "Ang Totoong Narco-list".

Advincula surrendered Monday evening to the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), said Philippine National Police (PNP) spokesperson Brigadier General Bernard Banac.

He underwent booking procedure at the CIDG office in Camp Crame, where he will also be detained until he is able to post P10,000 bail.

In the series of videos, the hooded man named Bikoy linked President Rodrigo Duterte's son Paolo, son-in-law Manases Carpio, former aide Christopher Lawrence Go and partner Honeylet Avanceña to illegal drugs operations.

Co was tagged as among the big time operators of an alleged drug den situated inside the Misibis Bay Resort.

Advincula first surrendered to the CIDG over charges of estafa and later posted bail.

At the time, he belied his statements on the video and tagged the government's critics, including then senator Antonio Trillanes and Vice President Leni Robredo as behind the videos.

Charges of sedition, cyber libel, libel, estafa, harboring a criminal and obstruction of justice have been filed against Robredo, Trillanes and several other personalities tagged as behind the videos. **(SunStar Philippines)**

Duterte administration hits back at claims president is involved in drug syndicate
==================================================================================

[![Image 1: Euan McKirdy](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/150103175015-euan-mckirdy-profile-new.jpg?c=16x9&q=h_270,w_480,c_fill/c_thumb,g_face,w_100,h_100)](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/euan-mckirdy)

By [Euan McKirdy](https://www.cnn.com/profiles/euan-mckirdy), CNN

4 min read

Published 10:44 PM EDT, Tue May 7, 2019

[](mailto:?subject=CNN%20content%20share&body=Check%20out%20this%20article%3A%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fwww.cnn.com%2F2019%2F05%2F07%2Fasia%2Fduterte-bikoy-philippines-unveiling-intl "Share with email")

Link Copied!

![Image 2: Davao City Vice Mayor Paolo Duterte, son of Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, and the president's son-in-law, Manases Carpio, take an oath as they attend a senate hearing in Manila on September 7, 2017.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/190507025016-paolo-duterte-01.jpg?q=x_4,y_251,h_2246,w_3991,c_crop/h_833,w_1480)

Davao City Vice Mayor Paolo Duterte, son of Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, and the president's son-in-law, Manases Carpio, take an oath as they attend a senate hearing in Manila on September 7, 2017.

Noel Celis/AFP/Getty Images

CNN  — 

Philippines President Rodrigo Duterte’s administration has strongly denied he has links to a drug syndicate, dismissing explosive allegations made by a man who went by the online pseudonym “Bikoy.”

In a series of five online videos entitled the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” (The real narco list), Bikoy – wearing a hooded sweatshirt to obscure his face – claimed to have documentary evidence that Duterte and his family members and close aides were deeply involved in the narcotics trade.

Duterte has waged a bloody and brutal war on drugs, which has seen thousands killed by police and vigilantes and which has sparked international condemnation.

As well as implicating the president, the man said the president’s son, the former Davao City vice mayor Paolo Duterte; former Special Assistant to the President Christopher “Bong” Go – now a senatorial candidate; and Duterte’s son-in-law, Manases Carpio – husband of Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte – were “players” in a drug syndicate.

All have denied any involvement with illegal drugs, with Go citing the president’s “hatred” of drugs as reason to stay away from the trade.

On Monday, the previously unidentified Bikoy allegedly outed himself as Peter Joemel Advincula, a heavyset man in his 20s or 30s with close-cropped hair and glasses.

Speaking at the offices for the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), the country’s national organization of lawyers, Advincula said his life was in danger after he implicated Duterte and those close to him.

Advincula claimed to have once been a part of the syndicate. Now wracked by guilt and hounded by death threats, he said he came forward to reveal his identity following the arrest of the webmaster of the site which first hosted the videos.

CNN has not been able to independently corroborate his claims that he is indeed the figure in the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” videos.

Politically sensitive timing
----------------------------

![Image 3: A poster of President Rodrigo Duterte's aide Bong Go is seen at an overpass as people take pictures of marching protesters during a rally at a road leading to Philippine Congress in Quezon City, east of Manila.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/190507025015-bong-go-01.jpg?q=w_1110,c_fill)

A poster of President Rodrigo Duterte's aide Bong Go is seen at an overpass as people take pictures of marching protesters during a rally at a road leading to Philippine Congress in Quezon City, east of Manila.

Richard James Mendoza/NurPhoto via Getty Images

The claims come just days before the country goes to the polls to elect lawmakers in mid-term elections. Their release has lit up social media in the Philippines, dividing opinion and sparking furious debate.

> > Are we in the verge of disclosing who are the real drug lords? [#Bikoy](https://twitter.com/hashtag/Bikoy?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [#DuterteDrugSyndicate](https://twitter.com/hashtag/DuterteDrugSyndicate?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [https://t.co/N3kIZhDMZf](https://t.co/N3kIZhDMZf)
> > 
> > — Gabrielle (@Gabgrielle) [May 6, 2019](https://twitter.com/Gabgrielle/status/1125293418110840833?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Government supporters say the allegations will backfire on opposition candidates. Others see the affair as spelling electoral disaster for candidates aligned with Malacanang, the presidential palace, and possibly criminal charges.

The chairman of the Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs, Panfilo Lacson, confirmed Tuesday that his panel would consider opening an investigation if Advincula provides a sworn statement. He added that compelling evidence must also be presented.

![Image 4: Supporters seen holding huge photos of opposition candidates.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/190507030039-otso-diretso-candidates-01.jpg?q=w_1110,c_fill)

Supporters seen holding huge photos of opposition candidates.

Josefiel Rivera/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images

In the videos, a hooded Bikoy said he used to work as an accountant for the syndicate operating in the southern Luzon and Visayas regions, “involved in recording transactions – how much money is allotted monthly per leader in the syndicate.”

He said he has complete records of these disbursements going back to 2010.

Advincula, speaking from the IBP, where he is seeking legal assistance and protection, said he decided to unmask himself because his past was gnawing at his conscience.

“I see the destruction of families due to drugs, of which I was once a part as a member of the syndicate. It is time to end the reign of this syndicate,” he said, according to [a translation from CNN affiliate](http://cnnphilippines.com/news/2019/5/6/Bikoy-reveal-identity.html) CNN Philippines.

‘Black propaganda’
------------------

Presidential spokesman Salvador Panelo described Bikoy’s claims as “black propaganda,” the official Philippines News Agency said, and dismissed the claims of the man on the grounds of his alleged past criminality.

“Information about the criminal background of Advincula is starting to come out. It appears that he has been incarcerated in 2012 for conviction of illegal recruitment and large scale estafa (fraud), as well as for theft,” the spokesman said in a statement Tuesday.

“Presently, there are news that he is facing multiple criminal cases like estafa, among others. These crimes involve moral turpitude that goes to the very integrity and credibility of Advincula or Bikoy,” he added.

In the videos, the man known as Bikoy claims to have indelible evidence. He alleges that Paolo Duterte has a tattoo which includes a code corresponding to his code name in the records – Alpha Tierra 0029.

Bikoy said Go, the senatorial candidate, also has a tattoo with a code which he has seen several times.

In response Go [showed his back publicly to prove he has no tattoo](http://cnnphilippines.com/news/2019/4/10/Bong-Go-drug-syndicate-dragon-back-tattoo.html). Panelo used the example as further evidence of Bikoy’s unreliability.

“There is a dictum in law which says: ‘You lie in one, you lie in all.’ This legal principle applies to Advincula or Bikoy,” the spokesman said.

So far Paolo Duterte has refused to show his back, CNN Philippines reports. He has admitted that he has a back tattoo, but has not confirmed or denied that it fits the description.

Panelo said there were “strong indications” that Advincula and Bikoy are the pawns of conspirators who seek to oust Duterte.

“Bikoy’s pretended fear for his life is part of the fraudulent act. Soon the pretenders and black propagandists will be unmasked,” the spokesman said.
