‘Bikoy’ to surrender to court in Quezon City
============================================

By: [Michael B. Jaucian](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/michael-b-jaucian) - Correspondent / [@mbjaucianINQ](https://www.twitter.com/@mbjaucianINQ)

[Inquirer Southern Luzon](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/source/inquirer-southern-luzon) / 03:29 PM February 16, 2020

Share:

[![Image 24: Copy Link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1229421/bikoy-to-surrender-to-court-in-quezon-city#)

[![Image 26: Bookmark](blob:https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/76f70cba1a4985ff842bd808acca549c)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1229421/bikoy-to-surrender-to-court-in-quezon-city#)

[![Image 28: Facebook](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1229421%2Fbikoy-to-surrender-to-court-in-quezon-city)

[![Image 30: X](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1229421%2Fbikoy-to-surrender-to-court-in-quezon-city)

[![Image 32: Peter Joemel or Bikoy](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/files/2020/02/received_1581041352058171-620x294.jpeg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/files/2020/02/received_1581041352058171.jpeg)Joseph Advincula sits with his brother Peter Joemel or “Bikoy” (left) who has decided to surrender to the Quezon City court Monday. Bikoy was charged with conspiracy to commit sedition over videos that linked President Duterte and members of his family to the drug trade where he featured as a hooded figure doing the expose. Photo from Joseph Advincula

LEGAZPI CITY — Peter Joemel Advincula, more popularly known by his alias “Bikoy”, will voluntary surrender to authorities on Monday to face the sedition case.

Joseph Advincula, younger brother of Bikoy, told the Inquirer Sunday that his older brother “will directly proceed to Metropolitan trial court branch 138 in Quezon City and will immediately post bail.”

_Article continues after this advertisement_

The Quezon City court on Friday ordered the arrest of former senator Antonio Trillanes IV and 10 others, including Advincula, over the widely circulated Bikoy videos that linked President Duterte and members of his family to the drug trade.

The younger Advincula said they will be in the area and will be accompanied by lawyer Larry Gadon.

Asked why not surrender to police as earlier planned, Joseph said “we are after his security”.

He said the family decided to surrender Bikoy because they respect the resolution of the Department of Justice on the sedition case.

“We are prepared for whatever consequences that may arise because we believe my brother is just a victim of the real \[person behind\] copy of narcolist video,” he said.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

He added that his brother was a victim of bad propaganda in his need for employment at the time.

“Gusto na din namin na umusad na ito upang maigawad na sa kung kanino nararapat ang hustisya (We also want this to move on so justice would be served to those who deserve it),” he said.

DOJ chief: Person arrested by NBI not ‘Bikoy’ videos uploader
=============================================================

By: [Darryl John Esguerra](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/darryl-john-esguerra) - Reporter / [@inquirerdotnet](https://www.twitter.com/@inquirerdotnet)

[INQUIRER.net](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/source/inquirer-net) / 04:56 PM May 02, 2019

Share:

[![Image 24: Copy Link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1113026/doj-chief-person-arrested-by-nbi-not-bikoy-videos-uploader#)

[![Image 26: Bookmark](blob:https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/76f70cba1a4985ff842bd808acca549c)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1113026/doj-chief-person-arrested-by-nbi-not-bikoy-videos-uploader#)

[![Image 28: Facebook](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1113026%2Fdoj-chief-person-arrested-by-nbi-not-bikoy-videos-uploader)

[![Image 30: X](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1113026%2Fdoj-chief-person-arrested-by-nbi-not-bikoy-videos-uploader)

MANILA, Philippines — The person arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) who was allegedly behind the video series accusing President Rodrigo Duterte’s family of involvement in the narcotics trade was not the uploader of the controversial videos, Justice Secretary Menardo Guevarra said Thursday.

Guevarra said a certain Rodel Jayme was taken into custody after the NBI conducted forensic examination on his desktop computer, mobile phones, and ISP billing statements and discovered that he was the “registrant and the administrator” of the website metrobalita.net that “constantly” publishes the link to the videos, which allegedly facilitated their circulation on social media.

**READ: [‘Totoong Narcolist’ uploader arrested – DOJ exec](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1112846/totoong-narcolist-uploader-arrested-doj-exec)**

_Article continues after this advertisement_

“It appears that he was the one who started all of this by creating the website behind the subsequent uploading of the Bikoy videos. It’s just logical that the NBI starts with him,” Guevarra said in a press briefing.

FEATURED STORIES

NEWSINFO

NEWSINFO

NEWSINFO

[Plunder, graft cases filed vs Recto, Ledesma over PhilHealth fund transfer](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157834/plunder-graft-cases-filed-vs-recto-ledesma-over-philhealth-fund-transfer)

NBI Cybercrime Division chief Victor Lorenzo also said that their investigation did not solely look into Jayme’s website but several accounts as well to gather more information.

“As of now, we’re still conducting a further evaluation on that matter. We’re not solely looking at metrobalita.net. Our investigation catered to several accounts also,” he said.

According to Guevarra, apart from charges for violation of the Cybercrime Prevention Act, Jayme may be slapped with charges for violation of the Anti-Child Abuse law.

The Justice chief also said Jayme voluntarily went to the NBI headquarters to clarify issues before his arrest and surrendered his devices and billing statements to the NBI Cybercrime Division agents who went to his residence to implement the search warrant at around 4 a.m. on April 30. /ee

An anonymous whistle-blower who appeared shrouded by darkness in videos accusing Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte’s family of taking millions from a drug syndicate has stunned the nation by revealing his identity.

The hooded figure known as Bikoy on Monday unveiled himself as a bald, round-faced man with glasses, after claiming in the clips that he used to keep financial records for a drug syndicate called the “Quadrangle Group” which included members of the president’s family and a close aide.

Peter Joemel Advincula said he was the man seen in five YouTube videos implicating the president’s son and former aide as “principal” operators in the country’s drug trade.

Reaction was swift from Malacanang Palace, the president’s official residence. Spokesman Salvador Panelo said: “As far as we are concerned, the video is black propaganda against the government.”

![Image 1: Duterte (right) with former presidential aide Christopher Go, who is also accused in the videos. Photo: AP](https://img.i-scmp.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=contain,width=1024,format=auto/sites/default/files/d8/images/methode/2019/05/07/76de6574-700c-11e9-b91a-87f62b76a5ee_1320x770_155714.JPG)

Duterte (right) with former presidential aide Christopher Go, who is also accused in the videos. Photo: AP

Advincula, who appears to be in his 30s or 40s, said he decided to surface so he could take legal action after he received death threats, and because his conscience weighed on him.

Misibis Bay Resort in Albay to file cyberlibel case vs ‘Bikoy’
==============================================================

By: [Neil Arwin Mercado](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/byline/neil-arwin-mercado) - Reporter / [@NAMercadoINQ](https://www.twitter.com/@NAMercadoINQ)

[INQUIRER.net](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/source/inquirer-net) / 07:20 PM May 06, 2019

Share:

[![Image 24: Copy Link](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1114538/misibis-bay-resort-in-albay-to-file-cyberlibel-case-vs-bikoy#)

[![Image 26: Bookmark](blob:https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/76f70cba1a4985ff842bd808acca549c)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1114538/misibis-bay-resort-in-albay-to-file-cyberlibel-case-vs-bikoy#)

[![Image 28: Facebook](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1114538%2Fmisibis-bay-resort-in-albay-to-file-cyberlibel-case-vs-bikoy)

[![Image 30: X](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsinfo.inquirer.net%2F1114538%2Fmisibis-bay-resort-in-albay-to-file-cyberlibel-case-vs-bikoy)

[![Image 32: Misibis Bay Resort in Albay to file cyberlibel case vs ‘Bikoy’ over drug accusations](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/files/2019/05/Peter-Joemel-Advincula-1-620x398.jpeg)](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/files/2019/05/Peter-Joemel-Advincula-1.jpeg)Peter Joemel Advincula (A.K.A.) Bikoy reads his statement at the IBP Multi Purpose hall at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines Ortigas, Pasig on May 06, 2019. PHOTO by Edwin Bacasmas/Philippine Daily Inquirer

MANILA, Philippines — The management of a resort in Albay said Monday they will file a cyberlibel case against ‘Bikoy’ for “maliciously and falsely” tagging the resort as a venue for illegal drug trading.

“Bikoy” is the hooded man in the “Ang Totoong Narcolist” videos that accused President Rodrigo Duterte’s relatives and allies of involvement in illegal drug activities.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

In one of the videos, “Bikoy” said Misibis Bay Resort is the “central house facility of Quadrangle Syndicate” and that the basement of the Misibis Bay Island Condominium serves as a drug laboratory.

FEATURED STORIES

NEWSINFO

[Magalong: Cabral’s last stop a probed project site](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157658/magalong-cabrals-last-stop-a-probed-project-site)

NEWSINFO

[Remulla clears Cabral's driver, raises 'red flags' vs husband](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157950/remulla-clears-cabrals-driver-raises-red-flags-vs-husband)

NEWSINFO

[Plunder, graft cases filed vs Recto, Ledesma over PhilHealth fund transfer](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2157834/plunder-graft-cases-filed-vs-recto-ledesma-over-philhealth-fund-transfer)

The resort, however, denied any involvement in the alleged drug trade and said that the claims were baseless.

“Misibis Bay is a first class, family-oriented resort. It has never been used as headquarters or as a front for any kind of illicit trade. Even claims that the resort allegedly uses one of its basements as a drug laboratory is false,” the company said in a statement.

The company said they invited members of the media and the police to check the only basement in the resort where a small kitchen is located.

“All other buildings and villas in the resort have no basement,” the company said.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

The company also denied the existence of a “control room” on the second floor of its newest building, saying that the whole floor is used as suite rooms for guests.

The company said the videos caused “irreparable damage” to the reputation of the resort.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

“The false and malicious allegations of Bikoy have caused irreparable damage to the reputation and good social standing of Misibis Bay and its owners for which reason he must be held criminally liable,” the company said.

A man named Peter Joemel Advincula, who claims to be “Bikoy,” surfaced at the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) on Monday afternoon.

Advincula said he went to the IBP to request legal assistance since he plans to submit an affidavit and file a case against the personalities he linked to the drug syndicate in the videos. /ee

Editorial

Conspiracy to commit what?
==========================

[Philippine Daily Inquirer](https://opinion.inquirer.net/source/philippine-daily-inquirer) / 05:08 AM February 13, 2020

Share:

[![Image 26: Copy Link](https://opinion.inquirer.net/single2017/images/copy-link.svg)](https://opinion.inquirer.net/127336/conspiracy-to-commit-what#)

[![Image 28: Bookmark](blob:https://opinion.inquirer.net/e8a57f4972516a1d3218894eabc89576)](https://opinion.inquirer.net/127336/conspiracy-to-commit-what#)

[![Image 30: Facebook](https://opinion.inquirer.net/single2017/images/fb-share.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fopinion.inquirer.net%2F127336%2Fconspiracy-to-commit-what)

[![Image 32: X](https://opinion.inquirer.net/single2017/images/x-share.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fopinion.inquirer.net%2F127336%2Fconspiracy-to-commit-what)

At the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group’s 67th founding anniversary celebration last Monday, Solicitor General Jose Calida declared that the filing of sedition complaints against several opposition figures, notably Vice President Leni Robredo, was a high point of his office’s cooperation with the Philippine National Police-CIDG.

“Truly,” he sermonized, “there is no crime more abhorrent than the betrayal of one’s country, aside from terrorism, sedition, inciting to sedition is committed and treason in the time of peace, more so when the traitor is an elected public official who before his or her assumption of office swore to defend and uphold the constitution. Thus, in its valiant attempt to fulfill the sacred oath to serve and protect the people, the PNP-CIDG filed sedition cases against respondents Vice President Leni Robredo, Mr. (Antonio) Trillanes and other well-known personalities who are responsible for the creation and release of the video ‘Ang Totoong Narcolist’.”

Mere hours after those remarks, however, the Department of Justice (DOJ) demolished Calida’s boast when it cleared Robredo and a number of other respondents of the charges. Exonerated with Robredo were six churchmen — Archbishop Socrates Villegas, Bishops Pablo Virgilio David, Honesto Ongtioco, and Teodoro Bacani, “running priest” Fr. Robert Reyes and former education secretary La Salle Br. Armin Luistro — along with 2019 opposition senatorial candidates Chel Diokno, Erin Tañada and Florin Hilbay, former senator Bam Aquino, former Magdalo representative Gary Alejano, senators Leila de Lima and Risa Hontiveros, and certain members of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

The charges against this virtual convention of supposed co-conspirators were all dropped for lack of evidence, according to the DOJ; or, as Undersecretary Markk L. Perete put it in more lawyerly wording: “In finding no probable cause for sedition or inciting to sedition, the \[prosecution\] panel found the element of public and tumultuous uprising wanting.”

FEATURED STORIES

OPINION

[God’s will, God’s way, God’s time](https://opinion.inquirer.net/188360/gods-will-gods-way-gods-time)

OPINION

[More measures against corruption](https://opinion.inquirer.net/188386/more-measures-against-corruption)

OPINION

[Dynasty, not evil per se; merely abused](https://opinion.inquirer.net/188384/dynasty-not-evil-per-se-merely-abused)

The same panel did, however, find probable cause to indict, for the lesser charge of “conspiracy to commit sedition,” 11 respondents, including former senator Antonio Trillanes IV; Catholic priests Fr. Albert Alejo and Fr. Flaviano Villanueva; and Peter Joemel Advincula, alias “Bikoy,” whose videos that were aired at the height of the 2019 election campaign season alleged that President Duterte’s relatives and close political allies were involved in the illegal drug trade.

The DOJ panel of prosecutors, in its 57-page resolution, said Trillanes et al. were indicted because, based mainly on Advincula’s testimony, they found “interlocking pieces of proof” that showed a “complete picture of the grand conspiracy between and among some respondents to create hatred or revenge against the President and his family with the end view of toppling and destabilizing the current administration.”

The downgraded charge against Trillanes et al., filed before the Quezon City Metropolitan Trial Court on Monday, has, however, left some legal experts scratching their heads.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

While the DOJ had dismissed charges of sedition, inciting to sedition, libel, cyber libel, estafa, and obstruction of justice against all respondents, including Trillanes, the former senator and a few others were still slapped with the complaint of “conspiracy to commit sedition” — despite the DOJ’s finding that there was “no probable cause for sedition or inciting to sedition.”

“If there is no finding of inciting to commit sedition because of absence of evidence on inciting the people to rise ‘publicly and tumultuously’ against the government, how then could there be a ‘conspiracy to commit sedition’?” asked a bewildered Mel Sta. Maria, dean of Far Eastern University’s Institute of Law, in a Facebook post.

“The most important element of sedition is public and tumultuous uprising. IF that element is not proven, there can be no sedition. And if there is no sedition, how can there be ‘conspiracy to commit sedition’? This is weird.”

_Article continues after this advertisement_

“ALL must have been exonerated,” he concluded.

It appears that throw anything against the wall and see which one sticks was the OSG-CIDG’s main battle plan in this Swiss cheese of a case designed to harass the opposition.

[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Since the win of President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") in the [2016 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election"), his [presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte") has been marked with controversy due to his crackdown on drugs and conflicts with organizations. Because of this, two attempts were allegedly made to oust him, namely the [Red October plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_/(plot/) "Red October (plot)") and the [Ang Totoong Narcolist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist "Ang Totoong Narcolist") videos. In response to the Ang Totoong Narcolist, a [matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix "Oust Duterte matrix") was made allegedly listing the figures wanting to oust Duterte.

The Red October plot was an alleged plot reportedly uncovered by Duterte on September 8, 2018. The numerous oppositions targeted said that the plot was fake. A [Chinese person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_people "Chinese people") was arrested on September 27 in [Teresa, Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teresa,_Rizal "Teresa, Rizal"), while schools were targeted for alleged participation in the plot. Next year, a former member of a drug syndicate created a YouTube channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" and uploaded five videos criticizing Duterte and his allies. The videos caused major controversy, leading the member of the drug syndicate and an opposition politician to be charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition").

Shortly after the YouTube channel made controversy, the Oust Duterte matrix was revealed by [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_/(Philippines/) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)") [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo"), targeting politicians and journalists who allegedly took part in an "ouster plot" against Duterte. Numerous figures included in the matrix denied their participation.

In an interview with [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler") in the late months of 2015, Duterte announced his candidacy for president in the upcoming 2016 Philippine presidential election.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-1) He filed his Certificate of Candidacy for the presidential election a few days later, withdrawing from the mayoral race of [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-2) After intense competition, he won with a total vote count of 16.6 million.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-3) His presidency was controversial, with his presidency marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people while carrying out thousands of raids. Because of this, he was involved in controversy against the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other organizations.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-4)

In Davao City, Duterte accused the opposition of creating an ouster plot on September 8, 2018, with opposition stating that he was a victim of his own "paranoia".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:0-5) A protest was planned during this time, but nothing happened in the supposed protest areas.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:0-5) Duterte accused soldiers of holding discussions with rebel groups like the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines") (CPP) and the [New People's Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_People%27s_Army "New People's Army") to oust him from office on September 24 in a military camp in [Jolo, Sulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolo,_Sulu "Jolo, Sulu"). The plot was allegedly named "Red October". The [Malacañang Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace"), the workplace of the president, released a video of his statement the next day.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-7) The day after that, the CPP said that the ouster plot was fake.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-8) Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo") stated that linking political opposition to ouster plots was a tactic used in [martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos") to silence the opposition.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-9) Senator Antonio Trillanes denied his involvement in the ouster plot.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-10) Four days later, the military seized from 13 alleged members of the CPP which had laptops and documents that Gen. [Antonio Parlade Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Parlade_Jr. "Antonio Parlade Jr.") alleged to be proof of the ouster plot.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-11) The Makabayan denied their involvement on September 27, although they were planning for a protest rally the next month.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-ro0622-12)

Youth activists denouncing [Armed Forces of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Philippines "Armed Forces of the Philippines") (AFP) terror tag and Red October plot, October 2018.

A Chinese person was arrested on September 27 in [Teresa, Rizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teresa,_Rizal "Teresa, Rizal"). The PNP raided her house and found firearms. Her house was allegedly used as a hideout for communist [guerillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerillas "Guerillas"). Some allegations were made that, during the arrest, the national bribed the officers with "protection money" so that she would not be arrested.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-13) A list of schools across [Metro Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Manila "Metro Manila") which were allegedly involved in the plot was released on October 4 by the AFP, with the military stating that the CPP was trying to "brainwash the students" into taking part in the activities. Among the list provided were the [University of the Philippines Diliman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Philippines_Diliman "University of the Philippines Diliman"), the [Ateneo de Manila University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateneo_de_Manila_University "Ateneo de Manila University"), the [De La Salle University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_La_Salle_University "De La Salle University"), and the [University of Santo Tomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Santo_Tomas "University of Santo Tomas").[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-14) The [Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Transportation_/(Philippines/) "Department of Transportation (Philippines)") said on October 7 that transport strikes were related to the plot. Department of Defense Secretary [Delfin Lorenzana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfin_Lorenzana "Delfin Lorenzana") said on October 12 that the plot fell apart. The military said that the plot would be moved to December, the 50th founding anniversary of CPP, although CPP President [Jose Maria Sison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison") denied these claims. The same month, nine farmers were killed in the [Sagay massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagay_massacre "Sagay massacre"), which authorities claimed was related to the plot.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:0-5)

Peter Joemel Advincula was born on March 22, 1989, in [Donsol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donsol "Donsol"), [Sorsogon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorsogon "Sorsogon"). His mother was a parish secretary while his father was a farmer. He pursued a degree in [philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy "Philosophy").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:02-15) His father died in 2009. On May 6 that same year, he was introduced to a drug [syndicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicate "Syndicate") operating out of [Misibis Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misibis_Bay "Misibis Bay"). He was tasked to prepare the monthly "TARA", a document listing the collections and payoffs that month. He was convicted of [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud") in 2012 and sentenced to six years in prison. He was released in 2017, one year early because of [good character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_conduct_time "Good conduct time").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:02-15) Wanting to become a [whistleblower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whistleblower "Whistleblower"),[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:02-15) he created a [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel named "Ang Totoong Narcolist" (transl. The True Narcolist) based around a former criminal named "Bikoy".[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:1-16) Five videos were created in total, between April 2, 2019, and Advincula's surrender on May 6.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-17) The videos accused Duterte-aligned figures, including Waldo Carpio, the brother of [Sara Duterte's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") husband, [Mans Carpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mans_Carpio "Mans Carpio"),[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:1-16) [Honeylet Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña") and her daughter Kitty Duterte,[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-18) and [Bong Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bong_Go "Bong Go").[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:2-19) Duterte-aligned politicians including [Presidential Spokesperson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_spokesperson_/(Philippines/) "Presidential spokesperson (Philippines)") [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") and Bong Go called the allegations false.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-20)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-21) Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") supported the videos.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-22) The [Liberal Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_/(Philippines/) "Liberal Party (Philippines)"), a part of the opposition, denied their involvement in the videos.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-23)

The DOJ started investigating the videos on April 17.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:5-24) Blogger Rodel Jayme was arrested in his residence in [Parañaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para%C3%B1aque "Parañaque") on April 30 for his alleged involvement in the videos.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:4-25) Jayme was charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition") on May 2.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-:5-24) Peter Advincula, the original 'Bikoy', surfaced on May 6. He asked for help from the [Integrated Bar of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Bar_of_the_Philippines "Integrated Bar of the Philippines") (IBP) to sue the Dutertes and their allies.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-26) The IBP rejected his offer.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-27) Advincula surrendered to police on May 23, stating that he played a role in a script made by the Liberal Party.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-28) The [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) started an investigation against Advincula on May 27.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-29) He turned himself in to the police for protection on June 3, suspecting that his life is in danger.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-30) The DOJ charged him with [fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud "Fraud").[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-31) He was released from protective custody on June 25.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-32) Politicians were sued for sedition on July 18, including Vice President Leni Robredo.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-33) Investigations were made into Robredo and other politicians' relation to the Bikoy videos.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-34) Advincula surrendered again to PNP on July 29.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-35) He posted the bail of 10,000 [PHP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_peso "Philippine peso") on July 31, getting released.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-36) Robredo responded to the investigation with a counter-affidavit, denying the accusations on August 29.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-37) On February 10, 2020, Robredo was cleared of her accusations while [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") was charged with sedition.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-38)

On January 20, 2021, Advincula was charged with [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") by a Manila court for allegedly false statements against the [Free Legal Assistance Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Legal_Assistance_Group "Free Legal Assistance Group"),[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-39) surrendering in a local police station in [Daraga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daraga "Daraga"), posting a 18,000 PHP bail.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-40) He allegedly killed three politicians in [Albay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albay "Albay") months later on November 13, with their bodies appearing in his _[ukay-ukay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukay-ukay "Ukay-ukay")_ store in Daraga. He was declared the primary suspect.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-41) He posted the 1 million PHP bail on December 16.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-42) In 2024, he filed his candidacy for senator in the [2025 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philippine_Senate_election "2025 Philippine Senate election") but was declared a [nuisance candidate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuisance_candidate "Nuisance candidate") by the [Commission on Elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Elections_/(Philippines/) "Commission on Elections (Philippines)").[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-43)

"Oust Duterte" matrix
---------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: \"Oust Duterte\" matrix")\]

After the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" YouTube channel caused controversy, a matrix was announced by Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo on April 22. 2019. The matrix allegedly contained the names of journalists and organizations who want to oust Duterte, with journalists from the [Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") (PCIJ) and [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler"). Panelo said that there was a "basis to release it" and that the matrix underwent "proper validation".[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-44) Another version of the matrix was released on May 8, with a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation to support the claims. The other version included "active online collaboration" between multiple opposition figures.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-45) Filipino Olympian [Hidilyn Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidilyn_Diaz "Hidilyn Diaz") was "shocked" over her inclusion in the matrix.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-46) Multiple major journalists claimed the matrix as "false". The PCIJ said the report was "wrong on many points". Rappler said that the report was an example of "how not to write an investigative report or even straight news."[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-47) Former journalists included in the matrix told the media about their inclusion.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-48) The National Union of Peoples' Lawyers asked the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") for government protection after harassment related to their involvement in the matrix.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-49) An editor for _[The Manila Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Manila_Times "The Manila Times")_ resigned on April 26 because the early article was "poorly sourced", later stating in an interview that he was asked to resign from the newspaper.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-50)

Other alleged plots
-------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other alleged plots")\]

A media report released on December 29, 2016, stated that ambassadors from the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") wanted to destabilize Duterte's government. In response to this, Duterte called the ambassadors "spies", although the United States government responded to the allegations as false.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-51) Paolo Duterte released a list on December 10, 2018, which contained people who allegedly wanted to oust Duterte including Vice President [Leni Robredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leni_Robredo "Leni Robredo"), former government officials, and journalists. The [Malacañang Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace") defended Duterte's list stating that there is no need to probe it. The list was eventually deleted.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-52) During the 72nd anniversary of the [Philippine Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Air_Force "Philippine Air Force"), Duterte pleaded for the military not to oust him. "I know that the Armed Forces and the Police will have to decide one day somehow. Do not do it please during my term," Duterte said.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alleged_ouster_plots_against_Rodrigo_Duterte#cite_note-53)

18.content:
[![Image 1: This is a good article. Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.")

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The **Oust Duterte** matrix was a diagram released on April 22, 2019, after the [Ang Totoong Narcolist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist "Ang Totoong Narcolist") YouTube channel controversy, where the channel speculated about the involvement of Duterte in drug syndicates. The diagram, released by the [Office of the President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace"), claimed to reveal links between journalists and organizations with plans to oust President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:2-1) It was officially released by Presidential Spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo"), who said that it underwent "proper validation." The matrix named journalists from multiple news websites, including the [_Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Center_for_Investigative_Journalism "Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism") and _[Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler")_. Another version was released on May 8 along with a [Microsoft PowerPoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_PowerPoint "Microsoft PowerPoint") presentation. People who were included in the matrix denied they had plans to oust Duterte. Following the release of the matrix, one of the groups sought government protection from harassment, while a newspaper editor resigned.

In an interview with [Rappler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappler "Rappler") in late 2015, Duterte announced his candidacy for president in the 2016 Philippine presidential election.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-2) He filed his Certificate of Candidacy (COC) for the elections a few days later, withdrawing from the mayoral race of [Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City").[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-3) After intense competition, he won with more than 16.6 million votes.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-4) His presidency was controversial, marked by an intensive crackdown on [illegal drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal_drugs "Illegal drugs"). In his [first 100 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Rodrigo_Duterte%27s_presidency "First 100 days of Rodrigo Duterte's presidency"), the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") (PNP) killed approximately 3,600 people, with thousands of raids conducted. Because of this, he was criticized by the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and other organizations.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-5) An [ouster plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_October_/(ouster_plot/) "Red October (ouster plot)") was announced by Duterte on September 8, 2018. It was allegedly planned by the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines"),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-6) which had previously assisted Duterte in the formation of his cabinet in 2016.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-8) After the announcement, the alleged plot "fell apart," according to politician [Delfin Lorenzana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delfin_Lorenzana "Delfin Lorenzana").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:0-9) A YouTube channel, named "[Ang Totoong Narcolist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ang_Totoong_Narcolist "Ang Totoong Narcolist")", was created in April 2019, alleging the involvement of Duterte in drug syndicates.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:1-10) Because of the videos, the alleged perpetrator and Senator [Antonio Trillanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Trillanes "Antonio Trillanes") were charged with [sedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedition "Sedition"), with the latter cleared of charges a year later.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-11)

Release and aftermath
---------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Oust_Duterte_matrix&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release and aftermath")\]

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/9f/OustDuterteMatrix.jpg/250px-OustDuterteMatrix.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:OustDuterteMatrix.jpg)

Presidential Spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") holding a copy of the matrix

After the "Ang Totoong Narcolist" YouTube channel caused controversy, a matrix was announced by presidential spokesperson [Salvador Panelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvador_Panelo "Salvador Panelo") on April 22. [Malacañang Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaca%C3%B1ang_Palace "Malacañang Palace"), the office of the President of the Philippines, was scheduled to publish the diagram officially, but [_The Manila Times_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Manila_Times "The Manila Times") beat them to it, prompting Panelo to question how the newspaper obtained it early.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:2-1) The matrix contained the names of journalists and organizations who allegedly want to oust Duterte, with journalists from the _Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism_ (PCIJ) and _Rappler_. Panelo said that there was a "basis to release it" and that the matrix underwent "proper validation," stating that "the President has so many sources, so he got the matrix from one of his sources." He also shared the possibility of the journalists "feeding their stories to the enemies of the state."[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-:2-1) Another version of the matrix was released on May 8, with a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation to support the claims. The other version included "active online collaboration" between former presidential spokesperson [Edwin Lacierda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Lacierda "Edwin Lacierda") and other people, journalist Ellen Tordesillas being part of "controversy" along with the [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_/(Philippines/) "Liberal Party (Philippines)") and the [Magdalo Party-List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalo_Party-List "Magdalo Party-List"), and other alleged links.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-12)

Filipino Olympian [Hidilyn Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidilyn_Diaz "Hidilyn Diaz") was "shocked" over her inclusion in the matrix. In a post shared on May 8, Diaz joked about her inclusion.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-13) [Maria Ressa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Ressa "Maria Ressa"), the CEO of _Rappler_, who was included in the matrix, said that it was "garbage" and a "Palace ploy to harass journalists." Ellen Tordesillas, an editor of [_Vera Files_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vera_Files "Vera Files"), which was also included in the matrix, denied the allegations, stating that it was "downright false." The PCIJ said the report was "wrong on many points," saying that they have never received an email from Tordesillas about the YouTube channel. The rest of Rappler said that the report was an example of "how not to write an investigative report or even straight news."[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-14) A former member of the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers, [Inday Espina-Varona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inday_Espina-Varona "Inday Espina-Varona"), and a former member of Vera Files, Luz Rumban, both said that they left their respective companies, with Rumban leaving in 2018.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-15) Magdalo Party-List Representative and opposition member [Gary Alejano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Alejano "Gary Alejano") branded the matrix as "utterly irresponsible" in a press briefing on April 22, demanding Panelo and Duterte resign over it.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-16) Numerous groups labeled the matrix as "ludicrous" and "dangerous".[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-17) Netizens mocked the creation of the matrix, stating that it lacked information. Some netizens made their own versions of the matrix with [Marvel heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Heroes_And_villains "Marvel Heroes And villains") and [cockroaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockroach "Cockroach").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-18)

Members of the National Union of Peoples' Lawyers were harassed for their security and safety. Through the union, they submitted an eight-page manifestation detailing this harassment to the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") and asked for government protection.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-19) An editor for The Manila Times resigned on April 26 because the first article was "poorly sourced." In an interview, the editor was allegedly asked to resign from the newspaper. He said that it could have been written in a journalistic manner but appeared to be "an opinion piece".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-20) According to opposition members, the matrix attempted to distract citizens from the upcoming [2019 Philippine general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Philippine_general_election "2019 Philippine general election") and allegedly attempted to "cripple the nation's democracy".[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-21) According to multiple groups, the matrix proved that the Duterte administration purposely shamed administration critics by alleging them to be government destabilizers.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oust_Duterte_matrix#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlemm_et_al.202365-22)

[Davao City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_City "Davao City"), Philippines



 |
| Alma mater | [Davao Doctors' College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davao_Doctors%27_College "Davao Doctors' College") ([BS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science")) |
| Occupations | Businesswoman, former nurse |
| Known for | [Domestic partner of the president of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spouse_of_the_president_of_the_Philippines "Spouse of the president of the Philippines") |
| Partner(s) | [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") (c. 1996–present) |
| Children | [Kitty Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte "Kitty Duterte") |

**Cielito** "**Honeylet**" **Salvador Avanceña** (born February 17, 1970[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-birthday-1)) is a Filipino businesswoman and former nurse who is the [domestic partner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_partnership "Domestic partnership") of [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte"), the 16th [President of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines") (in office from 2016 to 2022).[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-meethoneylet-2) Avanceña and Duterte have been in a relationship since as early as 1996 and have a daughter together. Although she was _de facto_ [spouse of the president of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spouse_of_the_president_of_the_Philippines "Spouse of the president of the Philippines"), she was not designated as [First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_ladies_and_gentlemen_of_the_Philippines "First ladies and gentlemen of the Philippines") during Duterte's presidency. Nonetheless, she served the duties of First Lady during [state banquets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_banquet "State banquet").

Avanceña first met [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") shortly after she participated in the 1988 _Mutya ng Dabaw_ [pageant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_pageant "Beauty pageant") where she finished as first runner-up.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-3) Avanceña worked as a nurse in the United States beginning in 2000,[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-INQCaruncho-4) returning to Davao shortly after her daughter Veronica ("Kitty") was born in the United States in April 2004.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-womanbehind-5)

She joined her partner's [presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte_presidential_campaign,_2016 "Rodrigo Duterte presidential campaign, 2016") in [Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon "Luzon") during the run-up to the [2016 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Philippine_presidential_election "2016 Philippine presidential election").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-womanbehind-5)

Prior to Duterte's presidency, Avanceña ran several businesses in Davao: a meat shop, a canteen catering service, and 11 [Mister Donut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mister_Donut "Mister Donut") franchises.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-womanbehind-5)

### Role in Duterte's presidency

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Role in Duterte's presidency")\]

Shortly after the inauguration of her partner as president, Avanceña was not named as [First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Ladies_and_Gentlemen_of_the_Philippines "First Ladies and Gentlemen of the Philippines"). Her stepdaughter [Sara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Duterte "Sara Duterte") was proposed to fulfill the role instead[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-Dutertewomen-6) but declined the offer.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-8)

Avanceña nevertheless fulfilled roles usually conducted by the First Lady, notably during the official visit of [Japanese prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Japan "Prime Minister of Japan") [Shinzo Abe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shinzo_Abe "Shinzo Abe") and the [30th ASEAN Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_ASEAN_Summits "2017 ASEAN Summits") in 2017.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-9)

### Post-Malacañang activities

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Post-Malacañang activities")\]

On March 11, 2025, Duterte was [arrested](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrest_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Arrest of Rodrigo Duterte") by the [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police") in coordination with [Interpol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpol "Interpol") and based on a warrant issued by the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") (ICC). During the arrest, Avanceña tried to persuade Duterte to not comply with police authorities due to her belief that they had no official warrant for him.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-DuterteFam_Airport_Distress-10) While Duterte was being held in custody at the [Villamor Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villamor_Air_Base "Villamor Air Base") in Pasay, an attempt by the police to block her daughter Kitty from reaching Duterte's room led to Avanceña hitting a [SAF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Action_Force "Special Action Force") officer on the head with her smartphone, allegedly in response to being separated from her daughter.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-ANC-11) The SAF officer was later hospitalized but soon recovered.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-ANC-11) The phone-striking incident by Avanceña has since been cited by ICC deputy prosecutor [Mame Mandiaye Niang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mame_Mandiaye_Niang "Mame Mandiaye Niang") as among the reasons for why the detained Duterte should not be granted interim release by the ICC to the country of his choice as it "risk\[s\] bringing real and substantial harm to the legitimate interests of victims and witnesses" in Duterte's case.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-13)

Avanceña became a partner of Duterte, then-married to [Elizabeth Zimmerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Zimmerman "Elizabeth Zimmerman"), in the late 1990s. With Duterte's infidelity, Zimmerman filed for an annulment before a regional trial court in [Pasig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasig "Pasig") in 1998, which was granted two years later.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-14)

Despite Avanceña being the common-law wife of Duterte since 2000, Duterte has admitted during his [2016 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Rodrigo_Duterte_presidential_campaign "2016 Rodrigo Duterte presidential campaign") to having multiple girlfriends such as a cosmetics worker in a shopping mall and a cashier.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-15) Others cited to have been among Duterte's partners during his relationship with Avanceña include [Agusan del Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agusan_del_Norte "Agusan del Norte") governor [Angelica Amante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelica_Amante "Angelica Amante"), former news reporter [Girlie Balaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girlie_Balaba "Girlie Balaba"), and presidential protocol director Jasmin Egan,[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-16)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-MNGallardo-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-18) while a rumor involving his alleged relationship with [agriculture undersecretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Agriculture_/(Philippines/) "Department of Agriculture (Philippines)") [Bernadette Romulo-Puyat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernadette_Romulo-Puyat "Bernadette Romulo-Puyat") was denied by Duterte.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-19) Avanceña previously denied Duterte's affairs in 2016, stating that she would have ended their relationship if they were true.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-INQCaruncho-4)

After Duterte assumed the presidency, Avanceña admitted to making uncomfortable adjustments to a more public life, with her expressing displeasure in having bodyguards for her and her daughter Kitty, stating that "I'm embarrassed in front of Davaoeños when they see so much security. We aren't used to it."[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a#cite_note-20)

Dueling conspiracy theories ignite the Philippines
==================================================

Alleged “Oust Duterte” plot aimed at toppling the president targets journalists and could presage a clampdown ahead of pivotal midterm elections

![Image 3](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=80&d=mm&r=pg) by [Jason Castaneda](https://asiatimes.com/author/jason-castaneda/) April 25, 2019February 18, 2020

![Image 4](https://i0.wp.com/asiatimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/Philippines-Rodrigo-Duterte-Effigy-Protest-November-30-2018-e1556183967851.jpg?fit=780%2C521&quality=89&ssl=1)

Activists burn an effigy of Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte near the US Embassy in Manila on November 30, 2018, Photo: AFP/Noel Celis

In the run-up to crucial midterm elections, Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte has accused his media and civil society critics of plotting to overthrow his government, a politically charged accusation that some fear could presage a severe new crackdown on dissent.

The alleged plot, first published in the Manila Times newspaper and likely based on information provided by the President’s Office, involves journalists who have allegedly attempted to “manipulate public emotion, touch base with the Leftist organization, enlist the support of the police and the military, then go for the ‘kill’ \[of overthrowing Duterte\].”

Presidential spokesman Salvador Panelo backed the validity of the conspiracy diagram published by Manila Times’ owner Dante Ang, a known Duterte ally and advisor, which exposed an alleged “matrix” of progressive groups and media personalities involved in an anti-government plot.

The spokesman claimed that the “Oust Duterte” matrix corroborates the president’s own intelligence findings, without elaborating.  
“The source of that is from the Office of the President. It’s from the President himself,” Panelo said on April 22 during a press briefing. “I was supposed to release it \[separately\] today,” he added, implying that there was no coordination with the Manila Times report.

In particular, the diagram accuses leading journalistic outlets such as Rappler, the Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism and the Vera Files, as well as the left-leaning National Union of People’s Lawyers (NUPL), which counts prominent opposition senatorial candidate Neri Colmenares among its ranks.

The accused journalists and lawyers have flatly rejected the matrix and related conspiracy as “a lie” intended to intimidate government critics and distract public attention from potential illicit activities by the presidential family and its closest allies ahead of hotly key elections next month.

PCIJ lashed out at the plot accusation for being “wrong on many points” and constituting a violation of the named journalists’ privacy.

“It offers tacit admission that these ‘experts,’ apparently working with the Office of the President had invaded the privacy of the emails and correspondence of journalists now being singled out,” the investigative organization said, questioning the legality of the report in an April 22 public statement.

Colmenares, meanwhile, threatened to sue the government on behalf of the NUPL. “It is an option on our part, collectively or individually, to file legal cases against those who are responsible for this latest script that is absurd, funny, hilarious, if not life-threatening to those whose names are listed in the matrix,” he said.

The conspiracy claim came days after the circulation of a series of videos entitled “Ang Totoong Narcolist”, or “the real narco list”, by an anonymous source known as “Bikoy.” The videos accuse the presidential family of years-long collaboration with Davao-based and international drug syndicates, including from China.

The anonymous source claims to be a former member of a drug syndicate with personal knowledge of the Duterte family’s alleged history of involvement in the illicit trade. He zeroed in in particular on Duterte’s son, Paolo Duterte, and his long-time personal assistant and senatorial candidate Bong Go.

Last year, Paolo Duterte resigned from his vice mayor position in Davao amid Senate investigations into his alleged involvement in the drug trade and ties with drug syndicates. He has consistently and strongly denied the accusations. In September 2017, Duterte told police to “kill” his son if the drug trafficking allegations were proven true.

![Image 9: Paolo Duterte, Davao's Vice Mayor and son of President Rodrigo Duterte, testifies at a Senate hearing on drug smuggling in Pasay, Metro Manila, Philippines, on September 7, 2017. Photo: Reuters/Erik De Castro](https://i0.wp.com/asiatimes-newspack.newspackstaging.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/Philippines-Paolo-Duterte-Drug-War-September-9-2017.jpg?resize=780%2C541&quality=89&ssl=1)

Paolo Duterte, Davao’s Vice Mayor and son of President Rodrigo Duterte, testifies at a Senate hearing on drug smuggling in Pasay, Metro Manila, Philippines, on September 7, 2017. Photo: Twitter

Still, the viral videos have undermined certain confidence in the tough-talking president, who has placed a scorched earth drug war at the heart of his policy agenda. Rights groups estimate as many as 16,000 suspects have been killed in the campaign.

His critics accuse him of not only widespread human rights violations, some of which have been taken up by International Criminal Court investigators, but also of a systematic cover up of the real roots of the country’s rampant and lucrative drug trade.

Certain opposition members have accused Duterte of orchestrating the drug war in order to conceal his family’s involvement in the illicit business as well as eliminate any competition. Duterte and his family members have steadfastly denied the unproven claims.

Enraged by the “Bikoy” videos, the president has apparently struck back with his own accusation of a coup plot against his perceived political enemies, which if proven could justify their incarceration on treason or other anti-state charges.

Significantly, Philippine security forces have been quick to question the veracity of Duterte’s and The Manila Times’ report of a conspiracy.

“There is always that possibility about groups wanting to oust him, but as of now we have not seen any specific threats likely to succeed to oust the president,” Armed Forces of the Philippines public affairs chief Colonel Noel Detoyato said on April 22.

Even the Philippine National Police (PNP), which has been largely subservient to the president and a key actor in implementing his controversial drug war, has been openly skeptical of the supposed plot.

“As of this time, we don’t have specific evidence on that,” PNP chief General Oscar Albayalde said. “But the police will always be on their toes, regardless of whether there is an ouster plot or not.”

![Image 11: Davao City mayor Sara Duterte-Carpio makes a point. Photo: Facebook](https://i0.wp.com/asiatimes-newspack.newspackstaging.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/Philippines-Sara-Duterte-Davao-City-Facebook.jpg?resize=780%2C589&quality=89&ssl=1)

Davao City mayor Sara Duterte-Carpio makes a point. Photo: Facebook

Duterte’s own daughter, Davao City mayor Sara Duterte, has also questioned the veracity of the alleged conspiracy to topple her father’s government.

“I don’t know if there has been a concerted effort, but let’s give the media entity the benefit of the doubt on what they choose to report and deem as deserving of coverage for the people” she said.

Vice President Leni Robredo, Duterte’s top political opponent, echoed that assessment. “This is the second matrix: if you remember, in the first destabilization matrix, I was included. And it wasn’t true.”

In 2018, Robredo, a lawyer and former social activist, was accused of involvement in a supposed conspiracy with leading businessmen to topple Duterte’s government and catapult her to power.

The list was circulated by Duterte’s son, Paolo, who at the time was facing accusations pursued by the Senate of his involvement in the drug trade. No action was taken against those identified on that plot list.

But with next month’s pivotal mid-term elections many seen as a de facto referendum on Duterte’s nearly three years in office, there are concerns the latest allegation could be leveraged to justify a clampdown to quiet rising anti-government criticism.

**Veronica Avanceña Duterte**[\[fn 1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-sur-1) (born April 10, 2004), often referred to as **Kitty**, is an American-born Filipino socialite who is the youngest daughter of former Philippine president [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") and his partner [Cielito "Honeylet" Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña"). She became a recognizable figure on social media during her father's presidency and has occasionally drawn media attention for her outspoken remarks and activities.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-Kami2-2)

On March 11, 2025, Duterte livestreamed and recorded the [arrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrest_of_Rodrigo_Duterte "Arrest of Rodrigo Duterte") of her father by police authorities at the [Ninoy Aquino International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninoy_Aquino_International_Airport "Ninoy Aquino International Airport") and at the [Villamor Air Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villamor_Air_Base "Villamor Air Base"), which were used by several news outlets due to the lack of media presence during the arrest.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-3)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-4)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-5)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-6)

Early life and education
------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kitty_Duterte&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")\]

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Rodrigo_Duterte_with_his_youngest_daughter_Veronica.jpg/250px-Rodrigo_Duterte_with_his_youngest_daughter_Veronica.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rodrigo_Duterte_with_his_youngest_daughter_Veronica.jpg)

Duterte with her father, Rodrigo Duterte

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e8/Veronica_%22Kitty%22_Duterte_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Veronica_%22Kitty%22_Duterte_/(cropped/).jpg)

Duterte in 2016

Kitty Duterte was born in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") on April 10, 2004, to Davao City Mayor [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") and nurse [Cielito "Honeylet" Avanceña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeylet_Avance%C3%B1a "Honeylet Avanceña"). Rodrigo himself had not visited the United States since the year 2000, having expressed disdain for the country since the [Evergreen Hotel explosion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Davao_City_Evergreen_Hotel_explosion "2002 Davao City Evergreen Hotel explosion") in Davao City in 2002.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-UR-7)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-8) Avanceña returned to the Philippines with Kitty shortly after the latter's birth.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-womanbehind-9)

Duterte studied at Stella Maris Academy in Davao City.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-Kami2-2) Attended University of the Philippines-Diliman studying Political Science.

Political involvement
---------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kitty_Duterte&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Political involvement")\]

### Incident during Rodrigo Duterte's arrest

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kitty_Duterte&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Incident during Rodrigo Duterte's arrest")\]

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Rodrigo_Duterte_oath_taking_6.30.16.jpg/250px-Rodrigo_Duterte_oath_taking_6.30.16.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rodrigo_Duterte_oath_taking_6.30.16.jpg)

Rodrigo Duterte takes oath as the 16th [President of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines"). Kitty Duterte is on the right of her father, holding the Bible

On March 11, 2025, during the arrest of her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, Kitty Duterte was heard cursing at then-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) Director General and former [Chief of the Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_the_Philippine_National_Police "Chief of the Philippine National Police") [Nicolas Torre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Torre "Nicolas Torre") in a video she posted on her Instagram account.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-auto1-10) Torre, who was explaining flight arrangements for Duterte, said he did not take offense at Kitty’s remarks, noting that he "had seen worse" and understood the heightened emotions of the situation.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-auto1-10)

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Duterte_siblings_in_2025.jpg/250px-Duterte_siblings_in_2025.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Duterte_siblings_in_2025.jpg)

Kitty Duterte (second to the left) and her paternal half-siblings during their visit to former President [Rodrigo Duterte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Duterte "Rodrigo Duterte") in [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") on August 27, 2025

In April 2025, Duterte, along with her half-brothers [Paolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Duterte "Paolo Duterte") and [Sebastian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Duterte "Sebastian Duterte"), filed a petition before the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines") seeking the return of their father from detention in [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") under the custody of the [International Criminal Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court "International Criminal Court") (ICC). She requested that the High Court hold oral arguments on the habeas corpus petition, arguing that the judiciary had a role in safeguarding constitutional rights in relation to foreign detention.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-11)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-12)

In May 2025, Honeylet confirmed that Rodrigo Duterte had urged Kitty to both continue her schooling and follow his career path after Kitty had expressed her reluctance to enter politics.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-GMAUntalan-13) Kitty campaigned for several of Rodrigo's endorsed candidates for senator in the [2025 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philippine_Senate_election "2025 Philippine Senate election"), citing her father's arrest as the reason for her active campaigning.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-GMAUntalan-13)

In August 2025, Duterte confirmed that her father had underwent a checkup and is in stable condition, and also she and along with her 3 half siblings visited their father in The Hague.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-14)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-15)

Duterte has cited her mother as a major influence and has expressed interest in pursuing careers in business or law.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-Kami2-2) She is also known to be a fan of international pop stars such as [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-Kami2-2)

In November 2023, One News reported that Kitty Duterte was in a relationship with [De La Salle Green Archers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_La_Salle_Green_Archers_basketball "De La Salle Green Archers basketball") guard [Evan Nelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Nelle "Evan Nelle").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-auto-16) Speculation about the couple’s relationship began prior to the start of the [UAAP Season 86](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAAP_Season_86_basketball_tournaments "UAAP Season 86 basketball tournaments") men’s basketball tournament, and Duterte was later seen attending La Salle games in support of Nelle.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-auto-16)

Beginning in 2022, a child named Mira ("Mimi", born 2019) is seen being raised by Kitty's parents, though there are conflicting reports on whether she is her sister or niece.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-17)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-18)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-19)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-20)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-21) She attributes the rose tattoo on her chest to Mira.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-22)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-23)

A week after her father's arrest in March 2025, several of her private [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") posts involving her alleged use of [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana") were leaked to the public, with the associated phrase "wake and bake" becoming viral.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-24)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-25)

Duterte is an American citizen.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-26) In April 2025, she was seen holding a United States passport while outside the Scheveningen penitentiary in The Hague, where her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, was detained. Responding to criticism online, Duterte maintained that she was a private citizen and did not need to explain her citizenship status, emphasizing that she was also a Filipino citizen.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitty_Duterte#cite_note-27)
